key_insight: EnterpriseClawBench turns real workplace agent sessions into a reproducible benchmark, making it possible to evaluate enterprise AI agents on tasks that mirror actual business workflows. It provides grounded tasks, fixtures, and semantic rubrics rather than synthetic test cases.
problem_solved: Current agent benchmarks often miss the complexity of real enterprise work, such as heterogeneous files, tool use, and strict business rules. This paper addresses the need for a realistic, reproducible evaluation set built from actual workplace sessions.
method: Collected enterprise agent sessions from a large proprietary archive of real workplace activity.
Reconstructed 852 reproducible tasks with recovered fixtures and rewritten prompts.
Annotated tasks with role classes, skill subclasses, hard rules, and semantic rubrics for structured evaluation.
impact: This benchmark gives AI/ML practitioners a more realistic way to measure how well enterprise agents perform in practical settings. It can improve model selection, debugging, and comparison for workplace automation systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing archived sessions transformed into benchmark tasks
Benchmark breakdown chart with 852 tasks across role and skill categories
Icon set for files, tools, workflows, and enterprise rules
Evaluation rubric graphic illustrating semantic scoring and hard constraints
paper_title: EnterpriseClawBench: Benchmarking Agents from Real Workplace Sessions
paper_authors: Jincheng Zhong, Weizhi Wang, Che Jiang, Kai Tian, Zhenzhao Yuan
